sources.entry: Build 30 things in 30 days with 30 tutorials

summary.title: JavaScript 30
summary.one_liner: You learn to build 30 small vanilla JavaScript projects, one per day, using browser APIs and the DOM without frameworks or libraries.
takeaways: Build 30 small projects in 30 days using only vanilla JavaScript, HTML and CSS, with no frameworks, compilers, libraries or boilerplate.
Projects cover DOM interaction and browser APIs such as Canvas, Speech Recognition, Speech Synthesis, Geolocation, LocalStorage and event delegation.
Suited to beginner-to-intermediate developers who already know some JavaScript; the author recommends a separate beginner course for fundamentals.
All 30 videos and starter files and completed solutions are available at once, and the tutorials are free.
summary.summary: JavaScript30 is a free series of 30 video tutorials by Wes Bos, where each day builds a small interactive project (for example a drum kit, CSS clock, canvas drawing, speech recognition, or a whack-a-mole game). The lessons deliberately avoid frameworks, libraries and opinionated patterns, relying on browser APIs and direct DOM work. The page lists all 30 days with starter files and completed solutions, and says the author spent over 300 hours on the series. The page also promotes the author's premium courses, which the rules here treat as marketing rather than content.
